## Cutting Through the AI Hype in Recruiting

Every recruiting tool now claims to be "AI-powered." But what does that actually mean for the daily work of talent acquisition professionals? We analyzed 50 AI recruiting tools to separate substance from marketing.

### What AI Does Well in Recruiting

| Task | AI Capability | Time Saved |
|---|---|---|
| Resume parsing and data extraction | Excellent | 90% |
| Boolean search query generation | Very Good | 80% |
| Interview scheduling | Excellent | 95% |
| Job description optimization | Good | 60% |
| Candidate rediscovery (ATS mining) | Very Good | 85% |
| Sourcing channel analytics | Good | 70% |

### Where AI Falls Short

| Task | AI Capability | Why It Fails |
|---|---|---|
| Assessing cultural fit | Poor | Culture is tacit, not data |
| Evaluating soft skills | Poor | Requires human perception |
| Candidate relationship building | Poor | Trust requires authenticity |
| Negotiation | Very Poor | Emotional intelligence needed |
| Executive-level assessment | Poor | Judgment, not pattern matching |
| Ethical decision-making | Very Poor | Values require human agency |

### The Optimal Human-AI Recruiting Stack

AI handles : Sourcing, screening, scheduling, analytics, reporting

Humans handle : Relationship building, assessment, negotiation, strategy, candidate experience

### The Productivity Multiplier

Recruiters using well-implemented AI tools can manage 40% more requisitions at equal or better quality. The key word is "well-implemented." Poor AI tools create more work through false positives, candidate alienation, and bias amplification.

### How TaaS Uses AI

Our subscription sourcing model combines AI-powered candidate identification with human relationship management. The AI finds the needles in the haystack; our recruiters build the relationships that close offers.
